content: {"rule": "K-C", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The judge text is a judge-seat evaluation of Matthew 1:16 as a pressed witness and resolves it by the verse's own ambiguity rather than by chain footing.", "verdict": "BREACH", "quote": "D1 vs C2 (Matthew 1:16): UNDERDETERMINED -- the passive egennēthē (was born) with feminine hēs (of whom) admits both the withheld-father and the birth-narration readings; the defender answered the beget-pattern and naming witnesses in [CR3] LINK 4 and [CR2] §5, and the challenger answered hēs in [DR3] C2.", "rule_words": "When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.", "room": "'weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse' — whether a single verse's ambiguity can make a link underdetermined or whether the judge must assess the competing chains by footing.", "why": "The judge text treats Matthew 1:16's own ambiguous wording as leaving the link underdetermined, which is verse-by-verse resolution rather than the chain-against-chain footing K-C requires."}
